items.definition:
tear or cut off the limbs of a person or animal
The predator began to dismember its prey.

act as a warning of (something bad)
The dark clouds forebode a coming storm.

completely destroy (a building, town, or other site)
The old factory was razed to make way for new apartments.

send (someone) back to their own country
The government decided to repatriate the refugees.

to withdraw formally from an alliance or federation
Several states threatened to secede from the union.

to waste time; to linger
Don't dally on your way home; it's getting late.

To prepare for battle; to place in a state of conflict.
The embattled government faced widespread protests.

To capture the fascinated attention of.
The magician's performance enthralled the audience.

pierce or transfix with a sharp instrument
The knight's spear was used to impale the dragon.

move or swing back and forth at a regular speed.
The pendulum continued to oscillate for a long time.

to take illegally or by force
The general tried to usurp power from the king.

To twist or squirm, especially in pain
He began to writhe in agony after falling.

to collect and combine (texts, information, etc.)
Please collate the reports before the meeting.

to join together; combine
The two rivers conjoin just before reaching the sea.

to make sad or dispirited; depress
The bad news seemed to deject him completely.

to express disapproval of
He tended to deprecate his own achievements, despite their significance.

to express contempt for; ridicule
The critics derided the play as amateurish and poorly written.

convert into an ion
High energy can ionize atoms.

to make someone less angry or hostile
He tried to placate the angry customer with a refund.

to assume as fact; to put forward as a basis for argument
She would posit that the theory is flawed.

to cause someone to adopt radical positions on political or social issues
The group tried to radicalize young people through online propaganda.

to make someone or something feel or look younger, fresher, or more lively
A good night's sleep can rejuvenate your mind and body.

make more noticeable or prominent.
Her new hairstyle accentuates her eyes.

to hypnotize or enthrall
The magician's performance completely mesmerized the audience.

to rob a place using violence, especially in wartime
The invading army began to pillage the conquered city.

to arrange or classify into strata or groups
The data was stratified by age group.

to reduce the force, effect, or value of
The vaccine helps to attenuate the effects of the virus.

to cause constipation
Certain medications can constipate you.

to make someone feel alienated or hostile
The government's policies began to disaffect the public.

to deprive someone of land, property, or other possessions
The landlord threatened to dispossess the tenants for unpaid rent.

to greatly astonish or amaze; to make speechless with amazement
The magician's trick dumbfounded the audience.

to cover (a surface) with a hard crust or coating
Over time, the pipes became encrusted with mineral deposits.

To place or deal with close together for contrasting effect.
The artist chose to juxtapose bright colors with dark shadows.

To make legitimate; to justify or make lawful.
The government sought to legitimize its actions through a public vote.

to treat (a person, group, or concept) as insignificant or peripheral
Society should not marginalize vulnerable groups.

to reject or void (a legal decision); to suppress
The court decided to quash the conviction.

to cause severe damage or destruction to
He wracked his brain trying to remember the answer.

to fasten or secure with battens
They had to batten down the hatches before the storm hit.

to ask someone urgently and fervently to do something
I beseech you to reconsider your decision.

to remove the testicles of a male animal or human
Farmers often castrate male livestock to improve meat quality.

Manipulate the boundaries of (an electoral constituency) so as to favor one party or class.
Critics accused the party of trying to gerrymander the voting districts.

to call or bring (someone) before a court to answer a criminal charge
The suspect was arraigned on charges of theft.

to besiege; to trouble persistently
The company was beleaguered by financial difficulties.

to give strength or energy to
A brisk walk in the fresh air can invigorate you.

to state one's opinion
He opined that the new policy would fail.

to read carefully
He spent hours perusing the documents.

hesitate or be unwilling to accept an idea or undertaking; (in baseball) an illegal motion by a pitcher
Many investors balk at the idea of putting money into risky ventures.

to project or support by a cantilever
The architect designed the balcony to cantilever out over the garden.

to describe or portray precisely
The architect tried to delineate the boundaries of the property.

to kill (a person or animal) painlessly to relieve suffering
The vet decided it was best to euthanize the suffering animal.

to experience something that is not real
Lack of sleep can cause people to hallucinate.

to secrete milk
Mammals lactate to feed their young.

to describe or regard as worthy of disgrace or great disapproval
Mental illness should not be stigmatized in society.

to be characteristic or a representative example of
His actions typify the spirit of generosity.

(of something bad) happen to (someone)
A great misfortune befell the family.

to hit or attack (someone) from the blind side; to surprise (someone) negatively
The news completely blindsided him.

to make immortal; to preserve in memory or fame forever
The artist hoped to immortalize the beauty of the landscape in his painting.

to untangle or fray
The old sweater began to ravel at the seams.

to give in; to abandon a harsh intention
After much persuasion, he finally began to relent.

to make holy or sacred
The priest will sanctify the new altar.

to conduct electricity with zero resistance
Certain materials can superconduct at very low temperatures.

Regard with great respect; revere.
Many cultures venerate their ancestors.

To form into crystals; to become clear or definite.
The sugar began to crystallize at the bottom of the pan.

to make clear; explain
Please elucidate the main points of your argument.
